title: Tech Note: Saving Data from a Non-Contextual Web Page
featured_technology: Web form input handling / record saving

historical_commentary.text: This note explains how to capture form input submitted from a 4D 'Non-Contextual' web page and save it into a 4D database table, a fundamental early-2000s dynamic web publishing pattern built on 4D's native Web server. The specific Non-Contextual web publishing model is tied to 4D's classic, pre-modern web architecture; the general concept of processing submitted web form data into database records remains completely relevant, but is now typically implemented using 4D's more capable, session/REST-oriented web frameworks rather than this era's Non-Contextual mode.
related_updates: 4D's web publishing model has evolved substantially since 2004, including session-based and REST/ORDA-based approaches for handling form submissions and persisting data
The specific 'Non-Contextual' web page mode described here reflects 4D's early web server architecture, largely superseded by later web server and web application development capabilities
